messages:
maya: Partner-ops raised a billing drift issue — small per-device rounding (~0.01-0.03 units/hr/device) becomes ~2-3% overage on large fleets.
aj: Do we have a concrete sample and invoice line?
maya: Sent a redacted event: `{ account_id: "acct_ABC", ts: "2026-03-11T08:22:00Z", usage_seconds: 0.48, units: 0.008 }` Partner says we billed 0.01 for this single event.
suresh: Suspect rounding order + float accumulation. We might be normalizing to minutes or rounding before summing.
oliver: Marketplace schema expects seconds (6-decimal precision). Partner sent 3 decimals; could be unit mismatch.
aj: I'll run a small sim (10k devices) with seconds vs minutes and integer vs float accumulation to reproduce.
suresh: Short-term mitigation: parse fractional seconds into integer microseconds (seconds * 1e6) and aggregate using integers until final billing round.
emily: Partner expects credits if we overbilled. Need billing/legal signoff and a backfill plan.
aj: Plan: PR today to change parser + unit tests; staging Wed, canary Fri. I'll own backfill script and post details to PD-9901.
maya: Also ask partner to switch to 6-decimal seconds and include explicit unit_type in webhook. Add schema validation to reject ambiguous payloads.
partner-delta-bot: Created ticket PD-9873: "marketplace usage rounding discrepancy - acct_ABC" assigned @aj (P2).
maya: Acceptance: 1) parser enforces unit_type, 2) internal integer micro-unit storage, 3) backfill + credit calc, 4) partner schema update and tests. Add billing metric: "monthly rounding drift by partner" to detect regressions.
aj: noted, will update PD-9873 with PR + canary plan.
file_meta: generated for training - simulated slack thread about marketplace metering rounding
